title: Masnavi i Ma'navi
author: rumi
attributionNote: The attribution is the one the edition and the scholarly consensus give; the catalogue does not adjudicate disputed cases.
description: Rumi's six-book poem of stories, dialogues and lyric passages, in which a tale about a king or a bird turns into an argument about the soul. Whinfield's English abridgement keeps the narrative sequence of all six books while shortening the discourses, so it is a reader's Masnavi rather than a literal rendering of every line.
historicalContext: Composed in Konya over the last two decades of Rumi's life and dictated to his disciple Husam al-Din Chelebi. The poem became the central teaching text of the Mevlevi tradition and one of the most widely translated works of Persian literature. Whinfield's abridgement was first published in 1898.
availabilityNote: Streamed from Wikisource page by page at read time. The 1898 translation by E. H. Whinfield is public domain; the page text is served by Wikisource under its own terms.
